findings.body: Two ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded and never used; the actual encoding is redone in the subsequent return statement, adding confusing dead code and needless allocation.
findings.failure_mode: Maintainability: readers may assume these lines have side effects; wasted work per invocation.
findings.impact: Two ASN1Encoder instances are created and written to, but their results are immediately discarded and never used; the actual encoding is redone in the subsequent return statement, adding confusing dead code and needless allocation.
findings.root_cause: Leftover scratch/experimental statements were left in the final implementation.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the two orphan ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) statements; only the writeDerSeq(...) return expression is needed.
findings.title: Redundant dead statements in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
findings.trigger: Any call to concatenatedRSToASN1DER executes these two lines.
findings.verifier_reason: Lines R114-R115 verbatim show `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` whose return values are discarded. The actual encoding happens in the subsequent return statement at R117-R121. These are indeed dead statements introduced by the patch - wasted allocations with no side effects.

pr.body:
…tory

closes #33831

This is the Keycloak main part for solving the https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/32962 and adding the related changes in the authz-client on the Keycloak side, which can then be later synced to the keycloak-client repository. 

In the end, I am using approach (2) from https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/32962 with adding the method `order()` to `CryptoProvider`, which allows to have multiple instances of `CryptoProvider` on classpath (Keycloak testsuite still uses the `DefaultCryptoProvider` as before this PR).

raw_findings.body: Such implementations fail to compile (source incompatibility) or throw AbstractMethodError at runtime because they do not implement the newly added abstract method.

raw_findings.impact: Such implementations fail to compile (source incompatibility) or throw AbstractMethodError at runtime because they do not implement the newly added abstract method.
raw_findings.root_cause: An abstract method was added to a public, ServiceLoader-based SPI interface without a default implementation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Provide a sensible default implementation (e.g. `default int order() { return 0; }`) instead of an abstract method to preserve backward compatibility for existing implementors.

raw_findings.body: debugf treats its first argument as a format string; a stray '%' in the built message would cause an IllegalFormatException / MissingFormatArgumentException instead of logging.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Potential formatting exception in the debug logging path.
raw_findings.impact: debugf treats its first argument as a format string; a stray '%' in the built message would cause an IllegalFormatException / MissingFormatArgumentException instead of logging.
raw_findings.root_cause: Dynamically built data string is passed where a static format string is expected.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use logger.debug(builder.toString()) (non-formatting overload) or pass the dynamic content as a format argument: logger.debugf("%s", builder).

raw_findings.trigger: detectProvider runs with more than one provider on the classpath and a provider class name that happens to contain a percent ('%') character.

finding.verifier_reason: Line R69 shows `logger.debugf(builder.toString());` where debugf expects a format string.
